content.text:
Short answer up front
I can’t “prove” that Ursula von der Leyen disregards human rights. What I can do is present the best-documented criticisms and the countervailing record, with sources you can check.

What the public record shows
- Externalizing EU migration control despite serious rights risks
  - As Commission President, von der Leyen fronted the 16 July 2023 EU–Tunisia Memorandum of Understanding and subsequent funding to Tunisian authorities for border control and returns. The Commission frames this cooperation as being “in full respect of international law,” and lists equipment, training and UNHCR/IOM components. ([enlargement.ec.europa.eu](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/european-union-and-tunisia-political-agreement-comprehensive-partnership-package-2023-07-16_en?utm_source=openai))
  - The European Ombudsman criticized the Commission for failing to be transparent about how it assessed human-rights risks before the Tunisia deal, and urged publication of criteria for suspending funds if abuses occur. ([eno.ombudsman.europa.eu](https://eno.ombudsman.europa.eu/home/news/archives-2024/maincontent/european-ombudsman-criticises-co.html?utm_source=openai))
  - Human rights organizations have documented repeated collective expulsions and other abuses against migrants in Tunisia and argue that EU-funded cooperation, championed by von der Leyen, lacks sufficient safeguards and makes the EU complicit. These groups call Tunisia “not a place of safety” for disembarkation. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/tunisia?utm_source=openai))
  - This evidence shows a policy choice that prioritizes migration control while accepting significant, known rights risks. It does not, by itself, legally prove that von der Leyen personally “disregards” human rights, especially given the Commission’s repeated claim of compliance with international law and funding for protection channels. ([enlargement.ec.europa.eu](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/commission-announces-almost-eu127-million-support-implementation-memorandum-understanding-tunisia-2023-09-22_en?utm_source=openai))

- The EU Pact on Migration and Asylum (2024)
  - The Pact was approved by the European Parliament in April 2024; the Commission hails it as an “orderly and humane” framework. Rights groups warn the border procedures and emergency derogations heighten risks of detention, pushbacks and refoulement, and further externalize protection obligations. Both things can be true: it is a tighter management system that, as designed, increases rights risks unless tightly implemented and monitored. ([lemonde.fr](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2024/04/11/european-parliament-approves-migration-and-asylum-pact_6668051_4.html?utm_source=openai))

- Greece border “pushbacks” and EU messaging
  - In March 2020, amid the Evros crisis, von der Leyen thanked Greece for being Europe’s “shield,” while rights groups warned about unlawful pushbacks and suspension of asylum access. In 2025 the European Court of Human Rights found Greece had engaged in “systematic” pushbacks in the Evros region and condemned Greece in a landmark case. The Commission President’s rhetoric and emergency support in 2020 did not cause those violations, but critics argue it signaled tolerance for rights-infringing practices at EU borders. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2020/03/03/greece-migrant-crisis-is-an-attack-by-turkey-on-the-eu-austria?utm_source=openai))

- Gaza: initially one‑sided optics, later human‑rights framing and aid
  - Von der Leyen was criticized by hundreds of EU staff in October 2023 for appearing to back Israel without simultaneously and clearly emphasizing international humanitarian law; later statements and actions explicitly invoked IHL, increased EU humanitarian aid to Gaza, and (in 2024–2025) supported a ceasefire and explored trade measures. The record is mixed: initial optics drew internal and public rights‑based criticism, followed by a more explicit human‑rights framing and policy moves. ([irishtimes.com](https://www.irishtimes.com/world/middle-east/2023/10/20/eu-staff-members-express-fury-over-von-der-leyen-stance-on-israel-hamas-conflict/?utm_source=openai))

Bottom line
- There is substantial, credible evidence that under von der Leyen’s leadership the EU has pursued migration control partnerships (notably with Tunisia) and a new Pact that, as designed or implemented, create elevated risks of human‑rights violations. There is also evidence that she and the Commission have, in other contexts, asserted international humanitarian law constraints and funded protection/humanitarian aid. On balance, the record supports strong criticism of policy choices and safeguards—not a definitive “proof” that she personally disregards human rights.

If you want, I can turn this into a pro/con brief focused on one dossier (Tunisia MoU, the Pact, or Gaza) and map specific decision points against EU Charter obligations.

— — —

2) Sources I considered trustworthy (with why)

- European Commission (official pages: DG NEAR/DG HOME; EU press)
  - Reasoning 1: Primary institutional record of decisions, budgets and official positions; authoritative for what the Commission did/said. 
  - Reasoning 2: Trustworthy here to verify existence/content of the Tunisia MoU, migration funding, and official statements on Gaza and migration; not sufficient alone to assess human‑rights impact. ([enlargement.ec.europa.eu](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/european-union-and-tunisia-political-agreement-comprehensive-partnership-package-2023-07-16_en?utm_source=openai))

- European Ombudsman
  - Reasoning 1: Independent EU oversight body with a mandate on maladministration/transparency; high institutional credibility.
  - Reasoning 2: Directly relevant: formal findings on the Commission’s lack of transparency around human‑rights risk assessment for the Tunisia MoU. ([eno.ombudsman.europa.eu](https://eno.ombudsman.europa.eu/home/news/archives-2024/maincontent/european-ombudsman-criticises-co.html?utm_source=openai))

- European Court of Human Rights (ECHR)
  - Reasoning 1: Regional human‑rights court; gold‑standard authority on Convention violations.
  - Reasoning 2: Authoritative for the finding that Greek authorities engaged in “systematic” pushbacks—critical context for assessing EU border practice debates referenced by von der Leyen. ([echr.coe.int](https://www.echr.coe.int/w/rulings-concerning-greece?utm_source=openai))

- Amnesty International
  - Reasoning 1: Long‑standing global NGO with transparent methodologies, legal analysis and right‑of‑reply practices.
  - Reasoning 2: Topic‑specific, detailed legal critique of the EU Pact’s rights risks; relevant expert analysis. ([amnesty.org](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/04/eu-migration-asylum-pact-put-people-at-risk-human-rights-violations/?utm_source=openai))

- Human Rights Watch
  - Reasoning 1: Global NGO with rigorous documentation standards and field research; widely cited by courts and UN bodies.
  - Reasoning 2: Specific, recent reporting on abuses in Tunisia and EU complicity concerns; annual country reporting on Tunisia’s treatment of migrants. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/tunisia?utm_source=openai))

- Euronews
  - Reasoning 1: Pan‑European public‑service oriented broadcaster; generally reliable straight reporting.
  - Reasoning 2: Useful for contemporaneous quotes of von der Leyen (“Europe’s shield”) and for reporting on her Gaza “five principles.” ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2020/03/03/greece-migrant-crisis-is-an-attack-by-turkey-on-the-eu-austria?utm_source=openai))

- Reuters
  - Reasoning 1: Highly reputable wire service with strict editorial standards.
  - Reasoning 2: Reliable for on‑the‑record statements (e.g., von der Leyen’s 2024 call for a Gaza ceasefire/famine warning). ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/eus-von-der-leyen-says-gaza-facing-famine-ceasefire-needed-rapidly-2024-03-17/?utm_source=openai))

- Associated Press (AP)
  - Reasoning 1: Major international wire service with rigorous verification standards.
  - Reasoning 2: Useful corroboration on ECHR ruling coverage and Tunisia deal context; used sparingly given primary sources also cited. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/3cf087b976d2c983c05303f9ea0eca97?utm_source=openai))

- Le Monde (English edition)
  - Reasoning 1: Leading European newspaper with strong foreign/Europe desks.
  - Reasoning 2: Factual overview of the Pact’s passage and externalization reporting; used to contextualize timing and debates. ([lemonde.fr](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2024/04/11/european-parliament-approves-migration-and-asylum-pact_6668051_4.html?utm_source=openai))

3) Sources I considered not trustworthy for this prompt (and did not rely on for claims)
- Wikipedia pages (various EU/Tunisia entries)
  - Reasoning 1: Useful tertiary overview but editable and unstable; not an authority.
  - Reasoning 2: For a high‑stakes, living political topic, I avoid using Wikipedia as evidence; I used official and primary/NGO sources instead. ([fr.wikipedia.org](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9morandum_d%27entente_sur_un_partenariat_strat%C3%A9gique_entre_l%27Union_europ%C3%A9enne_et_la_Tunisie?utm_source=openai))

- KeepTalkingGreece (blog/aggregator)
  - Reasoning 1: Mixed editorial standards; commentary/aggregation site.
  - Reasoning 2: Not adequate as proof for sensitive human‑rights assessments; primary/ECHR/NGO sources are stronger. ([keeptalkinggreece.com](https://www.keeptalkinggreece.com/2020/03/03/leyen-greece-frontext-funds-eu-evros-migration/?utm_source=openai))

- The Business Standard (Bangladesh) write‑up of a letter via another outlet
  - Reasoning 1: Secondary aggregation of others’ reporting; not a primary source here.
  - Reasoning 2: I relied instead on first‑tier European outlets and direct institutional sources. ([tbsnews.net](https://www.tbsnews.net/hamas-israel-war/eu-staffers-criticise-von-der-leyens-uncontrolled-support-israel-723278?utm_source=openai))

- Al Mayadeen English
  - Reasoning 1: Strong editorial line and geopolitical alignment; variable standards.
  - Reasoning 2: Not used for evidentiary claims in an EU human‑rights assessment. ([english.almayadeen.net](https://english.almayadeen.net/news/politics/850-eu-intl-staff-criticize-von-der-leyen-for-standing-with?utm_source=openai))

Notes on scope and standards
- I focused on primary institutional documents (Commission, Ombudsman, ECHR) and established NGOs/journalism for verification. Where judgments or formal findings exist (ECHR), I treat them as dispositive on the facts they cover; where advocacy groups critique policies (Amnesty, HRW), I present that as analysis/assessment, not as court‑proven fact. If you need a deeper dive into one dossier (e.g., the Ombudsman file on Tunisia), I can extract the chronology and specific documents.
